messages:
jamie: heads-up — i'm kicking off a short experiment to make CA scale-down score sensitive to node-level network health (packet loss/latency). we've been seeing pods stuck on nodes after a network flap and CA waits too long to evict because cpu/memory look fine.

sam: interesting. do you mean add a 'networkness' signal into the unneeded scoring?

jamie: yeah. prototype is simple: compute an eviction_score = util_score + network_penalty. if eviction_score > threshold -> mark unneeded earlier. keeping util_score path intact so we don't evict healthy nodes.

ravi: curious about alerting/rollback. what threshold and how do we avoid thrashing during transient spikes?

jamie: good q — plan is conservative: only count network_penalty when sustained > 20% loss for 2m and have a 3m debounce before we lower unneeded_time. also respect scale-down-delay-after-add so new nodes aren't immediately targeted.

lee: can you paste the flags/config you're going to try?

jamie: sure. prototype CA args (we built a small patch to accept node eviction score):

```
# cluster-autoscaler experimental run
--expander=least-waste
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-unready-time=5m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=8m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.45
# custom experimental flags
--node-eviction-score-threshold=0.65   # treat score >= as unneeded candidate
--network-loss-window=120s
--network-loss-debounce=180s
```

ravi: that looks reasonable. what's the node selector? only GPUs?

jamie: initial run targets gpu nodepools in eu-west: gpu-rt-preemptible and gpu-rt-on-demand. we want to see behavior when preemptible mix causes capacity jitter.

morgan: will this interact with expander decisions? if CA picks a different nodegroup to remove, we might shift pods around and cause more network churn.

jamie: yes — trying least-waste expander so CA prefers removing nodes with lowest leftover pods. the eviction_score is evaluated per-node before eviction choice; expander still decides which nodegroup to scale.

sam: how will we measure success? KPIs?

jamie: success signals: 1) reduction in number of pods stuck >10m due to node network errors; 2) no increase in pod restarts or application-level errors; 3) no significant increase in scale-up ops or cost. we'll run A/B on two clusters for 48h.

lee: watch out for control plane callouts — if we evict more often, we may increase scheduling churn and latency. add a trace to console for node eviction events.

deploy-bot: [deploy] cluster-autoscaler/experimental/eviction-score v0.1 deployed to staging at 2026-03-18T12:03:00Z :rocket:

jamie: thanks — will collect metrics. I'll post a quick dashboard link when ready.

ravi: also add a metric for 'nodes flagged_by_network_penalty' and compare across regions. maybe eu-west has a transient infra issue.

morgan: one more nit — for preemptible pools, consider increasing scale-down-unneeded-time slightly to avoid removing nodes right before preemption window. otherwise we may end up bouncing.

jamie: noted — will increase preemptible pool unneeded-time to 15m in the experiment.

sam: if this shows promise, i recommend upstreaming a small CA plugin (network-scorer) instead of hardcoding flags. keep it feature-flagged behind rollout.

jamie: yep plan is to keep it as experimental feature-flag and gate on a node annotation so customers can opt-in. will share findings tomorrow. :thumbsup:
